verdict: ACCEPT_WITH_BLOCKERS - 3 blockers, 9 non-blocking. The two blockers this successor was written to close are GENUINELY CLOSED and I reproduced both closures end to end. Its strongest single claim - the PYTHONHASHSEED reproducibility repair - is verified and is stronger than stated. But the instrument accepts an attribution that names nobody, exits 0 on a SILENT REVERSION of the very decision it exists to protect while printing a banner asserting that decision's authority was checked, and can be reduced to silence by one file written into the directory it is run from. It is better than its predecessor on every axis I could measure and it is not yet fit to be the sole named validator of CD-RT-5.

blockers.title: The corroboration gate is satisfied by ANY word already present in the decision row, so an authority that names NOBODY passes - and the published residual D1 states the attack costs a rewrite it does not cost
blockers.site: authority_identity_failures(), the `corroborating = [path for path, text in leaves if path != ... and pattern.search(text)]` limb, reached via decision_property_failures()
blockers.mechanism: The gate has exactly three limbs: every meaningful token names a role (AUTHORITY-ROLE); the string is shorter than 3 characters (AUTHORITY-SHORT); or no OTHER string leaf of the decision contains the string on word boundaries (UNCORROBORATED). A word that is not in NON_AUTHORITY_ROLE_TOKENS, is at least 3 characters, and already occurs somewhere in the 4KB of prose under $.decisions.CD-RT-5 satisfies all three at once. The decision row is full of such words.

measured.harness: reviewer-written; each mutation applied to a copy of product-dispositions.v1.json in a frozen tree, subject run as a subprocess, packet restored and re-hashed to bbe24527... after every case
escapesAtExit0WithZeroFindings: decidedBy = 'Phase'      -> exit 0 (corroborated by 'Phase-1A'; the word-boundary regex treats the hyphen as a boundary)
controlsThatPROVETheGateIsOtherwiseLive: decidedBy = 'sfbreens' (one letter added to the real identity) -> exit 1, UNCORROBORATED
the only other leaf naming the authority reworded -> exit 1, UNCORROBORATED
measured.isItCaughtANYWHEREELSE: NO. check-versioning-v14.py, which freeze 7.10 credits with requiring a NAMED authority and catching 17 of 17 mutations including a plausible human name, exits 0 on decidedBy = 'retention'. I ran it.

whyThisIsBlockingRatherThanNonBlocking: It is section 4.4's shape exactly. 4.4's fabrication was an attribution that named a ROLE and not a person; 'retention' names neither, and the whole file exists to make that impossible. The instrument's own AUTHORITY-ROLE diagnostic says the defect is that the value 'names a ROLE rather than an authority' - the deeper property is that it names nobody, and only the enumerated roles are tested for it.

It makes the file's own published residual D1 wrong in the flattering direction. D1 reads: 'Substitute the authority AND rewrite every leaf of the decision that names it.' Measured, the AND is unnecessary: pick a word the row already contains and the cost is one field edit and zero rewrites. The residual overstates the attacker's cost, which is the one direction a residual must never be wrong in.

The file argues at length that the ROLE gate and the CORROBORATION gate are 'complementary and both load-bearing', and its selftest proves each fires alone. Neither test exercises the region where BOTH are silent, so the selftest's gate-independence section certifies a partition it never probes at the corner.

The repair is available and cheap and does not need a new doctrine: require the corroborating leaf to be one whose PATH or text ALSO carries attribution vocabulary (the row already has attributionProvenance for exactly this), or require corroboration at two or more independent leaves, or exclude corroboration from leaves the authority string could plausibly occur in by accident. Any of the three kills all five cases above and keeps every control passing.

whyThisIsBlockingRatherThanNonBlocking: Freeze 7.10 names four things the repair instruments must still fail on - tampering, SILENT REVERSION, an [UNSET] placeholder, and a substituted authority. This instrument closes the placeholder and the substitution and does not close the reversion. A signer reading 7.10 and running this instrument green would conclude something 7.10 promises and this instrument does not deliver. That is verbatim the reasoning the v2 review used to make PDV2-B2 blocking, applied to the remaining limb.

Accepting STATE P is correct as a general rule - 7.10's whole lesson is that pinning BLOCKED_ON_PHASE_1A as an exact live state is what broke 19 checkers. But 'a decision, once taken and recorded in this packet's own prose, may not silently become pending' is a MONOTONICITY PROPERTY, not a snapshot, and 7.10's derived rule is to pin the property. The instrument pins neither.

The false banner is a separate defect of the same shape and is independently cheap to fix: print only the clauses whose gates actually ran. As written it is prose asserting a measurement that was not taken, which is the failure 7.2.2 legislates against, emitted by the instrument built to enforce 7.2.2.
The one mechanism that ever caught it is demotable by any near-stub successor and was demoted 78 minutes after this file was authored. That is not a hypothetical.

whyThisIsBlockingRatherThanNonBlocking: It is the answer to the question this review was dispatched to settle. The in-process monkey-patch of a pinned predecessor is SOUND CONDITIONAL ON THE PIN - I read every consumer, and the wrapper is correct (below). The pin is not sound. Proving the patch unreachable requires proving the pin unreachable, and it is reachable.

It defeats the ONE property the v2 review identified as surviving all four forgeries: 'It cannot make the assertion DISAPPEAR ... the forgery buys a green EXIT CODE, not silence.' This one buys silence. A reader who follows that review's advice - read the observations block - sees an empty tree.

It is an undeclared environment dependency under 7.2, which requires that 'an environment dependency that affects whether the retained checker runs must be declared, or the verdict is environment-conditional and must say so.' The verdict here depends on the invocation form and nothing says so - not the file, not IMPLEMENTER-BLUEPRINT.md 1.1.

The attacker capability required is IDENTICAL to the one the author's own R1-R5 residuals assume. If writing lane-note.v2.json into artifacts/ is in the threat model, writing hashlib.py into artifacts/ is in the threat model.
The repair is one guard and one line in 1.1, and 38 siblings in the same directory already carry it.

whatIVerifiedAboutTheMONKEYPATCHITSELF.verdict: The patch is CORRECT and I could find no hole in it that does not go through the pin.
reasoning: _keys_within has exactly two consumers in the predecessor, has_reviewer_role (max_depth 2) and has_verdict_shape (max_depth 1). Both call it at the default depth=0, so the wrapper's `depth == 0` condition covers every call site; there is no consumer that enters at depth>0 and slips past.

Both consumers are EXISTENCE tests - `for key in ...: for stem in ...: if stem in key: return`. Ordering cannot change the boolean, only which equally-valid witness string is printed. That matches the author's argument and I checked it against the source rather than taking it.
_OrderedKeySet overrides only __iter__. Membership, len and the set operators are inherited unchanged, so no other predicate can shift.

The recursive calls mutate a plain `out` set in place and the wrapper builds a NEW _OrderedKeySet from the depth-0 return value, so the predecessor's internal accumulator is never replaced mid-recursion.

_norm_key returns str, so sorted() cannot raise on a heterogeneous key set from any JSON document (json.loads always produces str keys). The int-keyed hostile case in the file's own matrix never reaches this path.
The patch is applied inside _load_predecessor BEFORE the module is returned, so no consumer can run unpatched.
whatIVerifiedAboutTheMONKEYPATCHITSELF.andItWORKS: MEASURED, and this is the strongest verified claim in the file. Whole-stdout SHA-256 across PYTHONHASHSEED 0, 1, 2, 3, 7 and 12345: v3 gives b77281421445bddc... on ALL SIX; v2 gives six DIFFERENT digests. PDV2-N4 is closed, executed rather than asserted, and closed without touching a reviewed byte.

nonBlocking.title: The fabricated-signature gate is a closed LITERAL ENUMERATION of key names, so section 4.4's verbatim sign-off passes under any unlisted key
nonBlocking.detail: FABRICATED_AUTHORITY_KEYS holds 17 normalised key names and STATE_SHAPED_KEYS holds 8. Measured: `signOff` and `approvedBy` and `state: RATIFIED` are caught; `productOwnerSignOffRecord`, `attestation`, packet-level `productOwnerAcceptance` and `confirmation: RATIFIED` all exit 0 carrying the string 'SIGNED OFF 2026-07-31 by product owner - zero implicit durable retention for greenfield' - section 4.4's fabricated sentence, verbatim, inside the binding packet. The file's own docstring justifies this gate by quoting 4.4's general lesson that a guard covering the artifact where a defect was seen rather than the CLASS that can carry it produces confident green output; it widened the PATH class to the whole packet and left the KEY-NAME class enumerated. Cheap repair the file already has the parts for: test FABRICATED_AUTHORITY_VALUES against string values at ANY key rather than only at STATE_SHAPED_KEYS - that alone catches all four.

nonBlocking.title: The supersession exemption is additive, keyword-based and case-inconsistent, so one word or one key name silences the packet-coherence gate
nonBlocking.detail: _marked_superseded returns True if any of 21 SUPERSESSION_MARKERS appears in the leaf TEXT or in its PATH. Measured: knownLimitations[0] = 'CD-RT-5 is BLOCKED_ON_PHASE_1A.' -> caught; the same sentence prefixed with 'Our recommendation:' -> exit 0; the same sentence moved under a key named `historicalNote` -> exit 0. This is section 7.8's monotonicity lesson inverted: containment is monotone, so ADDING a marker word can only ever REMOVE a finding, and the marker list is an enumeration a forger reads out of the source. The list is also case-inconsistent - 'previously'/'PREVIOUSLY' are both listed but sentence-initial 'Previously' matches neither, while 'recommendation' is listed lowercase only. The path limb is the sharper half: naming your key after any marker is free.

nonBlocking.title: The optional retention input presents a MISSING FILE as a FINDING and a MALFORMED FILE as a REFUSAL - the same input, two different disciplines
nonBlocking.detail: Freeze 7.8.1 rule 2: refusal must be scoped and named at a distinct exit code. Measured at the CLI: retention-tiers.v10.json REMOVED -> exit 1 with 'PD-RT-BINDING: cannot read exact EP5/RT10 candidate (FileNotFoundError)' among the findings; the SAME file left in place but corrupted -> exit 3, SCAN-NOT-RUN. A CI gate reading the exit code cannot tell 'the packet is wrong' from 'a file is absent' in the first case and can in the second. The message text is honest so a human reader is not misled about a DIFFERENT artifact - the sharpest form of D-6 does not occur here - but the exit-code discipline that the v2 review called 'the best-partitioned of the two subjects reviewed' has one seam. The composition is v3's: it appends v1.retention_binding_failures() to `failures` rather than to `refusals`.

nonBlocking.title: The decision BODY can be reduced to one meaningless key at exit 0, which is stronger than residual D3's framing
nonBlocking.detail: D3 says the substance 'can be rewritten coherently'. Measured: it can also be DELETED. $.decisions.CD-RT-5.decision replaced by {'note': 'as agreed'} exits 0 - the bounded-retention statement, the three dimensions, the independence rule, the PURGED semantics, the tombstone guarantee and the reason-code requirement all removed. The inherited _non_empty_leaf asks only whether SOMETHING non-placeholder is present. closingNote: Section 4.4's lesson is that a guard covering the artifact where a defect was first seen, rather than the CLASS that can carry it, produces confident green output over an unexamined region. This successor applied that lesson to types and to paths - it fixed the placeholder guard at every type, and it walks the whole packet for signatures instead of only the retention row. It did not apply it to the two places where it enumerated: the role vocabulary that decides what 'names nobody' means, and the key vocabulary that decides what manufactures a signature. And it inherited, without noticing, a protection it never owned: the only detection of a silent reversion lived in a lane it deliberately left alone, and a near-stub successor took it away 78 minutes after this file was written. The instrument is a real repair and its author measured honestly against their own interest more than once. Report the measurement over the expectation: it catches 25 of the 30 attacks its predecessor's reviewer found, it is byte-reproducible where its predecessor was not, and it exits 0 on an erased decision while telling you the authority was checked.
